This guide serves as a comprehensive developer manual, outlining Daany's features, functionality, and usage, as well as a listing of related papers.

I challenge the conventional view of Galileo's influence on science by suggesting that he struggled with mathematical proficiency, thereby outsourcing key calculations to other luminaries of the time, like Bonaventura Cavalieri and Johannes Kepler. This perceived weakness led Galileo to focus on experimentation and data analysis, which, although valuable, were not enough to establish his scientific legacy. It's proposed that Galileo's reliance on others' mathematical expertise contributed to his core idea of inertia, which he then wrapped in a philosophical framework to make up for his mathematical shortcomings. Ultimately, his scientific breakthroughs were possible only through a collaborative effort, one that highlighted the limitations of his own scientific capabilities.

The increasing popularity of Tsallis' thermodynamic framework is evident from its applications across various fields. It addresses a critical limitation of Boltzmann's statistics by incorporating correlations, which is significant in the context of the Hubble's discovery. Researchers have been motivated to analyze non-Gaussian properties of ionization during the early universe using a Tsallis-based framework. Building on this trend, analysts have found that the framework accurately reproduces the Bose-Einstein and Fermi-Dirac distributions as a special case of $q=1$. The early universe' s ionization is analyzed using a Tsallis-based distribution with the assumption that the electron density follows a power law. By substituting this density into the Saha equation, the solution for $q$ is derived analytically in the context of neutral and recombined reactions. The results show that the value of $q$ decreases as the universe becomes ionized and then stabilizes at a very small value, confirming cosmological equilibrium. Moreover, the advantages of Tsallis statistics over Boltzmann statistics in terms of convergence are verified.

The analysis of magnetic reconnection, a collisionless process, necessitates complex, computationally intensive kinetic models, contrasting with more feasible fluid-based simulations. Our study utilizes the Magnetohydrodynamics with Adaptable Embedded Particle-in-Cell (MHD-AEP) model to investigate the interaction between two magnetic flux ropes by comparing two simulation methods. One involves integrating the Vlasov-Poisson equations within a fully kinetic approach, while another uses an embedded Particle-in-Cell model that merges kinetic and fluid elements, with the interface determined dynamically based on an optimized criterion. By evaluating various indicators including electron temperature, magnetic field irregularity and entropy, as well as the formation of mirror islands, we observed comparable outcomes from both methods that were also supported by similar physical principles. Our study demonstrates that the embedded P-In-C model can effectively capture the core of collisionless Reconnection at a relatively lower computational cost of $\sim 10$ times that of a fully kinetic approach, showcasing its value in high-C Courant number simulations of magnetic reconnection.

This document provides a summary of the content from a course held at Stanford University in the spring of 2018.  The course brings together insights from cognitive neuroscience and systems neuroscience to create intelligent systems by combining human and machine intelligence.  The course uses a tangible example - a digital assistant that learns and improves over time as it helps a software engineer by understanding the nuances of their thoughts and actions.  As the assistant carries out tasks such as coding, bug-fixing, and planning, it develops a deeper understanding of its partner's thinking, eventually becoming capable of reading the programmer's mind.  The course explores the implications of this assistant's capabilities - does it respect its partner's privacy, or does it take advantage of them?  By studying the dynamics between humans and machines, we can learn new system designs that learn and adapt in an equitable and fair manner.
